metadata.title: Claude Code, Opened.
metadata.subtitle: What's actually in Anthropic's public repo — the honest inventory
metadata.purpose: Walk the anthropics/claude-code GitHub repo with real cloc/git data and show that the 'source code' most people assume is there is not. The load-bearing artifact is a 5,248-line CHANGELOG and a set of community plugins. The compiled binary ships separately. That finding is the lesson.
metadata.source: anthropics/claude-code cloned 2026-08-01; all data computed via git log, find, wc -l. See REPO-VERIFY.md.
metadata.notes: Kokoro am_onyx, free (IN-FOR-BEAR LAW). GATE P before any ElevenLabs swap. Deep-explainer on ai-explainer chassis. 4 acts, 15 body beats. beats.narration_text: Annyeong — this is Liam, in for Bear. Anthropic's Claude Code has a public GitHub repo. Everyone assumes it's the source code. We're going to clone it, count the files, and see what's actually load-bearing. The answer is not what you think.
beats.new_visual_element: Claude composer — ask lands answered: 'cloning anthropics/claude-code…' → 210 files. No src. No dist. Let's open it.

beats.narration_text: Extension breakdown — the actual inventory. One hundred and six Markdown files. That is half the repository. Twenty-one shell scripts. Twenty-one Python files. Eight Terraform configuration files. Five TypeScript files. Zero compiled JavaScript. Zero dist folders. This is not a source repo.

beats.narration_text: Folder inventory confirms it. CHANGELOG.md — 5,248 lines. README.md — 72 lines. Then examples, plugins, scripts, dot-claude commands. No src directory. No dist. No compiled output anywhere. If you came looking for the internals, the repo says plainly: they are not here.

After the tree is done, two red lines appear with ✗ symbol: '  ✗  src/  (NOT FOUND)' and '  ✗  dist/  (NOT FOUND)' — each ✗ is crimson. Pause 1s on the two red lines.

beats.narration_text: The five TypeScript files are in scripts/ and they're not the tool — they're the issue tracker. Auto-close duplicates. Triage labels. Issue lifecycle. Sweep. This is GitHub maintenance code, not Claude Code internals. The source is not here. That's the finding.

After all five appear, a terracotta label slides in below: 'Purpose: GitHub issue management — not the tool.' The column reads like a receipt.

beats.narration_text: The CHANGELOG is 5,248 lines and documents 353 releases — from version 0.2.21 to 2.1.220. At this cadence, Anthropic is shipping Claude Code roughly twice per day. That is the real clock in this repo. Not the commit count. Not the file count. The release velocity.

verify.source: grep '^## [0-9]' CHANGELOG.md | wc -l && grep '^## [0-9]' CHANGELOG.md | head -1 && grep '^## [0-9]' CHANGELOG.md | tail -1

Then a timeline annotation draws in: 'v0.2.21 ─────────────────────── v2.1.220' with 'oldest' and 'newest' labels. Finally a terracotta annotation box slides in: '~2 releases/day'. The number 353 stays large on screen as the annotations appear around it.

beats.narration_text: The commit log has 222 entries across six months. Here's the monthly split. February through July 2026. Two bars per month — total commits in ink, bot commits in terracotta. The bot is a GitHub Actions job that updates CHANGELOG.md every time a release fires. It dominates every month.

production_viz.label: grouped bar chart — total / bot / human per month

Each group has TWO bars: total (tall, ink, semi-opaque) and bot (terracotta, drawn INSIDE the total bar, showing overlap — bot is a subset). Human count labels appear in terracotta above each group. All bars grow simultaneously from 0 after a 0.3s delay. Month labels along x-axis in SERIF. Y-axis from 0 to 55. After bars settle: 'Bot: 176 / 222 = 79%' annotation draws with arrow.

beats.narration_text: Strip the bot: 46 human commits in six months. Not a slow team — this is a public surface repo mirroring internal releases. The actual development is happening elsewhere, in a private codebase, and arriving here only as CHANGELOG entries when the bot fires.

beats.narration_text: But the plugins folder is worth your time. This is ralph-wiggum — its Stop hook blocks Claude's exit and re-feeds the same prompt if the completion promise hasn't been delivered. Real bash that ships in the repo. Readable. Adaptable. This is what you can actually run.
